data.summary: The plan front‑loads the student’s weak units (2, 4, 6) while still moving through the AP Calculus AB curriculum. Each week includes a concrete set of tasks that fit within the 8‑hour limit, and live classes are slotted exactly when they occur. The final week is reserved for mixed review and timed free‑response practice.

weeks.focus: Build a solid foundation in Unit 2 differentiation basics.
tasks: Attend live Class 11300 (2 hrs).
Complete the class worksheet on average and instantaneous rates (1 hr).
Do 12 FRQ practice problems on defining derivatives and notation; check answers with the scoring guide (2 hrs).
Create a one‑page summary sheet of definitions and notation (1 hr).
Watch a 30‑minute Khan Academy video reviewing rates of change (0.5 hr).
Practice estimating derivatives from tables for 5 new functions (1.5 hr).

weeks.focus: Finish Unit 2 fundamentals and begin limits (Unit 1).
tasks: Read textbook sections 2.3‑2.5; take notes on the Power Rule and continuity (1 hr).
Complete 10 derivative‑practice problems using the Power Rule (1 hr).
Do 8 limit‑estimation problems from graphs and tables (1 hr).
Write a brief explanation of how differentiability implies continuity (0.5 hr).
Complete the AP‑style FRQ set on differentiation and limits (2 hrs).
Review class notes from Week 1 and correct any errors (0.5 hr).
Spend 2 hrs on timed mixed practice covering topics 1.1‑2.5.
Read and annotate the textbook sections on the Chain Rule and Implicit Differentiation (1 hr).
Watch a 45‑minute video demonstration of the Chain Rule with several examples (0.75 hr).
Solve 12 Chain Rule problems, including one with a trig function (1.5 hr).
Complete 8 implicit differentiation problems, checking work against solution key (1.5 hr).
Do 4 FRQs that combine chain rule and implicit differentiation; grade with rubric (1 hr).
Create a cheat‑sheet of derivative formulas for composite functions (0.5 hr).
Review previous weeks’ notes and redo any incorrect problems (1.75 hr).

weeks.focus: Contextual applications of differentiation – start Unit 4.
tasks: Attend live Class 11301 (2 hrs).
Summarize class examples on interpreting derivatives in context (0.5 hr).
Complete the class worksheet on straight‑line motion (1 hr).
Do 10 FRQs on motion contexts (position, velocity, acceleration) (2 hrs).
Practice 6 rate‑of‑change problems in non‑motion contexts (1 hr).
Create a set of real‑world scenarios and write the derivative interpretation for each (1 hr).
Review Chain Rule notes to ensure ability to differentiate applied functions (0.5 hr).

weeks.focus: Analytical applications – extrema and first‑derivative test (Unit 5).
tasks: Read textbook sections on Mean Value Theorem and Extreme Value Theorem (1 hr).
Complete 8 problems locating critical points and classifying extrema (1.5 hr).
Do a worksheet on the First Derivative Test (1 hr).
Solve 6 FRQs that require using the MVT or EVT (2 hrs).
Create a one‑page flowchart for deciding which test to use on a given function (0.5 hr).
Review Unit 4 applications by re‑doing 4 motion FRQs (1 hr).
Spend 0.5 hr on timed mixed practice covering topics 4.1‑5.4.
Attend live Class 11302 (2 hrs).
Summarize class notes on accumulations and Riemann sums (0.5 hr).
Complete 10 Riemann‑sum problems with different sample points (1.5 hr).
Watch a 30‑minute video on the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (0.5 hr).
Do 8 problems applying the FTC to compute definite integrals (1.5 hr).
Practice 6 FRQs that combine area approximation and FTC (2 hrs).
Review cheat‑sheet of integration notation and compare with differentiation results (0.5 hr).

weeks.focus: Mixed review and timed AP‑style practice.
tasks: Take a full 90‑minute timed FRQ practice exam covering all units (1.5 hrs).
Grade the practice exam using the official scoring guidelines; note weak areas (1 hr).
Do a targeted review packet: 2 problems each on limits, derivatives, chain rule, related rates, extrema, FTC, differential equations, and average value (2 hrs).
Create a concise “big‑ideas” sheet for each unit (1 hr).
Review any remaining class notes or worksheets that were missed earlier (1 hr).
Spend 0.5 hr on quick mental‑recall drills (key formulas, theorems).

data.final_week_advice: Focus on pacing and accuracy during timed practice, use the error log from the mock exam to do a final quick‑fire review of any lingering gaps, and keep a calm, confident mindset for the actual AP exam.
